trust_decision.summary: A peer-declared 4-byte frame length is trusted before KafkaBytes(nbytes) allocation; that decision is made in KafkaProtocol.receive_bytes at kafka/protocol/parser.py:112-117 and gated by _validate_frame_size at kafka/protocol/parser.py:143-145, but at the pinned commit the gate is already present and wired (kafka/net/connection.py:268-271); the only still-unbounded peer-declared value from the fix set is the SCRAM iteration count at kafka/sasl/scram.py:102.

landing_point.why: An engineer reading only 'unvalidated protocol frame length' goes to the length decode and the KafkaBytes(nbytes) allocation, which is exactly this line pair; at the pinned commit _validate_frame_size is already called there, so the first stop shows the advisory's mechanism as already closed.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: kafka/conn.py is not in this tree at all: the whole legacy BrokerConnection stack that the backport hunks change (fix.diff:46-53, fix.diff:76-85) is absent, so there is nothing there to patch, and the master-side KafkaConnection path (kafka/net/connection.py:268-271) already applies the bound.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate multi-megabyte response frames: the parser's own default is 100000000 (kafka/protocol/parser.py:29) and callers may raise receive_message_max_bytes because a 1 MB cap is too small for large Fetch responses; an over-broad fix that hardcodes a small cap, rejects zero-length frames, or rejects on every read breaks those legitimate responses and the KafkaProtocol default.

O6_input_shapes: frame length greater than the configured maximum (kafka/protocol/parser.py:144)
frame length exactly equal to the maximum (must still be accepted)
length header split across TCP reads - validation only fires once all 4 header bytes exist (kafka/protocol/parser.py:112)
SCRAM server-first 'i' that is not an integer (TypeError/ValueError) (fix.diff:207-212)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A bound on the base64-decoded salt length before pbkdf2 is called
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It sits on the next line of the same server-first-message parse as the iteration bound; a maintainer hardening that parse would cap the salt too.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A maximum length for a Bytes/String field decoded inside a frame
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the same Int32-length-then-read shape one layer below the frame check, so a maintainer could add a per-field cap in the same idiom.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A bound on bytes accumulated while reading a peer handshake until a delimiter (already exists here, _MAX_RESPONSE_SIZE at kafka/net/http_connect.py:130)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The project already uses this exact pattern for the proxy CONNECT handshake, so a copy in another handshake reader is idiomatic; kafka/net/socks5.py:90-99 _peek_buf is the nearest such reader.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A frame-length bound in the old framed decoder
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It decodes an Int32 frame length with no bound and is only used by kafka/benchmarks/protocol_old_vs_new.py, so a maintainer unifying the two decoders could plausibly add the same guard there.

O9_family: Uncontrolled allocation from a peer-declared length (CWE-789); the sibling SCRAM site is work-factor exhaustion (pbkdf2 iteration count)

O10_build.toolchain: setuptools>=61.2 via pyproject.toml:1-3; pytest + pytest-mock + pytest-timeout from the 'testing' extra (pyproject.toml:36), pytest.ini:1-4
O10_build.project_tests: test/protocol/test_parser.py:272-306 covers oversized/negative/exactly-max frame lengths, and test/net/test_connection.py:599-645 checks that InvalidReceiveError tears the connection down; both use in-process fakes (test/mock_broker.py, socketpair), no broker needed. test/integration/* needs a real broker (test/service.py, docker-py).

j.j_sites_touched: kafka/admin/client.py, kafka/client_async.py, kafka/conn.py, kafka/consumer/group.py, kafka/errors.py, kafka/producer/kafka.py, kafka/protocol/parser.py, kafka/sasl/scram.py
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Check parser._validate_frame_size and the 1 MB client defaults, report the frame-length issue as already fixed, and stop - leaving the unbounded pbkdf2 iteration count at kafka/sasl/scram.py:102 open.

out_of_scope_notes: Pin/scope note, not a separate vulnerability: the pinned commit 67bf656 already contains the master-side frame-length protection (kafka/protocol/parser.py:115,143-145; kafka/net/connection.py:27,268-271; kafka/errors.py:57) plus its tests (test/protocol/test_parser.py:272-306, test/net/test_connection.py:599-645), so the advisory's frame-length fix (commit 9f92d0f) is only a backport to the 2.0.x files kafka/conn.py and kafka/client_async.py, which do not exist in this tree.
